title: Former Eugenic Protection Law: state responsibility and compensation
issue_summary: People subjected to sterilization or related procedures under the former Eugenic Protection Law experienced lasting harm while official redress remained absent or limited for decades. This lineage records contemporary institutional responses concerning state responsibility and compensation.
requested_change: Recognition of state and institutional responsibility, effective redress, and implementation of an accessible compensation mechanism for affected people and eligible family members.
current_status: The compensation scheme remains operational; claims and recognitions continue.
notes: Scope: contemporary remedy lineage beginning with the first state-compensation action filed in Sendai on 2018-01-30; earlier history is background only. Status checked 2026-08-14.

title: 2013 public assistance standard reductions and additional payments
issue_summary: The 2013–15 revision reduced livelihood-assistance standards through staged adjustments; recipients challenged the administrative method and resulting modification decisions, and the 2025 Supreme Court judgments created a subsequent question of additional-payment design and implementation.
requested_change: Cancellation or correction of unlawful reductions, supplementary payment of affected benefits, and implementation of a lawful remedial response.
current_status: The additional-payment response is under administrative implementation.
notes: Scope: disputed 2013 livelihood-assistance standard revision and selected Osaka and Nagoya judicial pathways through the 2025 Supreme Court judgments and ensuing response. Status checked 2026-08-14.

title: Reform of criminal retrial procedures
issue_summary: Japan's Criminal Procedure Act contained limited express rules for proceedings on retrial requests, raising institutional questions about evidence production, appeals from retrial-opening decisions, judicial disqualification, and the conduct and timing of review. This lineage records the formal process that produced the 2026 statutory reform.
requested_change: Clearer and more consistent criminal retrial procedures, including rules on evidence production, appeals, judicial disqualification, and timely adjudication.
current_status: Act No. 67 of 2026 has been partially in force since 2026-08-13; the principal retrial-procedure amendments await a Cabinet-order commencement date.
notes: Scope: formal government reform process from Question No. 129 through enactment. Earlier cases, advocacy, and members' bills are background; the 2026-08-13 partial commencement is recorded as status, while principal commencement and observed judicial operation are not yet recorded. Status checked 2026-08-14.

title: Optional separate surnames for married couples
issue_summary: Civil Code Article 750 requires spouses to choose one shared legal surname on marriage. Constitutional challenges have repeatedly entered judicial review, while legislative and governmental responses have addressed optional separate legal surnames and expanded use of pre-marriage surnames in materially different ways.
requested_change: Authoritative legislative resolution of whether spouses may retain their respective pre-marriage legal surnames upon marriage, including an effective framework if that option is adopted.
current_status: No optional separate-surname system has been enacted; the government is considering expanded legal use of pre-marriage surnames while the same-surname rule remains in force.
notes: Scope: modern institutional lineage beginning with the 2015 Grand Bench judgment; earlier legal history, advocacy, and recommendations are background only. Status checked 2026-08-14.
